research_question: At the same first-approach-relative stage, can deployment-observable history predict whether pickup stall will be confirmed within the next 20 steps?

event_rule.name: pickup_stall_approach0.10_w40_move0.04
event_rule.target: task target selected from privileged simulator state for labels only
event_rule.confirmation: maximum target 3D displacement from the first-approach pose remains < 0.04 m for 40 steps
event_rule.one_shot: only the first approach is evaluated; later transport/placement proximity cannot create a pickup event

window.positive: pickup stall is confirmed exactly 20 steps after the pilot checkpoint
window.negative: at the pilot checkpoint the target has not yet moved 0.04 m, then it crosses 0.04 m during the following 20 steps
window.checkpoint_stage_constraint: exclude negatives whose target crossed 0.04 m on or before the checkpoint; otherwise the predictor can solve the task by reading already-completed pickup progress
window.stage_baseline: Fit an analysis-only baseline from first_approach_step and privileged target displacement at the checkpoint. The primary model comparison is deployment features versus this stronger stage baseline.
window.claim_boundary: The pilot predicts imminent stall confirmation after 20 observed stall-development steps; it is not pre-attempt failure prediction.

information_boundary.predictor_inputs: RGB and/or proprioception/action history through the pilot checkpoint only
information_boundary.forbidden: Privileged scene state may not enter predictor features or normalization statistics.

split.stratification: Classify groups as mixed, all-positive, or negative-only. For each stratum with at least three groups, allocate round(20%) to validation, the same count to test, and the remainder to train. Keep all-positive groups in train so validation/test positives always support same-initial-state contrasts.
split.revision_note: The initial positive-vs-negative-only allocation gave test same-state-negative coverage 4/9, so the pre-training split was revised using label strata. The first pilot model then exposed a stricter temporal-label flaw: some negatives had already moved 0.04 m by the checkpoint. Those samples are excluded and the first model result is invalid. On the strict cohort, integer rounding assigned only one of eight mixed groups to test; before strict-model training, allocation was frozen as 4/2/2 mixed groups so both evaluation splits retain two same-state contrast groups.
split.selection: model and threshold selection use validation only; test is evaluated once

physical_review.sample: 12 deterministic review episodes covering all 11 event-positive initial-state groups
physical_review.reviewed_by: human visual review of synchronized main/wrist contact sheets
physical_review.decision: freeze event rule for pilot dataset construction

gate.remaining_requirement: at least 80% of positives must retain an aligned negative under the frozen grouped pilot split/evaluation design
